verdict.rationale: Flagsmith ships its own background automation for flag changes. Release Pipelines move flags through stages automatically using triggers and actions, and can auto-generate change requests. Scheduled flags queue a change and apply it at a future time without anyone being present. Both are limited to flag-rollout workflows, and scheduled flags are a one-off future action, not a recurring schedule. missing for 10: recurring/cron-style schedules, general-purpose automations beyond flag rollouts, detailed documentation of trigger types, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
Release Pipelines act as your intelligent release assistant, automating your entire feature flag deployment process.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production, eliminating manual effort and streamlining your deployment workflow.
Scheduled flags allow you to queue and automatically apply changes to feature flags at a specified future time, eliminating the need for manual intervention at the exact moment of change.
